column1: # Kinematic chain for the MX850 — 5-axis mill, trunnion-table layout.
# Units: millimetres and degrees, Z up (same as every chain TSV).
# 21-column format (obj_file + mesh_off/mesh_rot). Two chains branch off the
# upper base: the table slide stack (X -> B -> C) and the spindle stack
# Operator-confirmed parts:
#   DOC1231B -> base_floor   (Fixed, chain root)
#   DOC1228A -> base_upper   (Fixed, on base_floor)
#   DOC1227B -> X            (Linear, carries the trunnion)
#   DOC3184A -> B            (Rotary, swinging support for the rotary table)
#   DOC3186A -> C            (Rotary, the rotating table itself)
#   DOC1230A -> Y            (Linear, spindle Y slide)
#   DOC1234B -> Z            (Linear, spindle Z ram, carried by Y)
# motion_axis mapping (matches kernel): X=0, Y=1, Z=2, B=3, C=4.
# obj_file column holds the plain basename — the machine files live flat
# alongside this TSV in machines/, and on the SD card they land flat at
# /system/machine/. render::obj::lookup("MX850-DOC1227B.STL") rewrites to
# `system/machine/MX850-DOC1227B.STL` and hits the VFS cache directly.
# STL vertices are in one shared assembly frame, so the fixed and linear
# links need no offsets. The rotaries do: a joint rotates about its own
# origin, so each rotary's origin sits on its axis and mesh_off moves the
# STL back by the same amount (the assembly is unchanged at B=C=0).
#   C axis: centre of the 629 mm table (DOC3186A bounding box), top face
#   B axis: runs along X; y/z least-squares fitted to the trunnion and
#           carriage bearing bores (DOC3184A / DOC1227B), ~±3 mm  ->
#           y=1114.05 (same as the table centre), z=986.0. x is arbitrary on
#           the axis; 1364.0 keeps C's offset purely vertical.
# Confirm both against the machine drawings before trusting sim clearances.
